414: /// Replaces `\r\n` with `\n` in-place in `src`.
415: pub fn normalize_newlines(src: &mut String) -> LineEndings {
416:     if !src.as_bytes().contains(&b'\r') {
417:         return LineEndings::Unix;
418:     }
419: 
420:     // We replace `\r\n` with `\n` in-place, which doesn't break utf-8 encoding.
421:     // While we *can* call `as_mut_vec` and do surgery on the live string
422:     // directly, let's rather steal the contents of `src`. This makes the code
423:     // safe even if a panic occurs.
424: 
425:     let mut buf = std::mem::replace(src, String::new()).into_bytes();
426:     let mut gap_len = 0;
427:     let mut tail = buf.as_mut_slice();
428:     loop {
429:         let idx = match find_crlf(&tail[gap_len..]) {
430:             None => tail.len(),
431:             Some(idx) => idx + gap_len,
432:         };
433:         tail.copy_within(gap_len..idx, 0);
434:         tail = &mut tail[idx - gap_len..];
435:         if tail.len() == gap_len {
436:             break;
437:         }
438:         gap_len += 1;
439:     }
440: 
441:     // Account for removed `\r`.
442:     // After `set_len`, `buf` is guaranteed to contain utf-8 again.
443:     let new_len = buf.len() - gap_len;
444:     unsafe {
445:         buf.set_len(new_len);
446:         *src = String::from_utf8_unchecked(buf);
447:     }
448:     return LineEndings::Dos;
449: 
450:     fn find_crlf(src: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
451:         let mut search_idx = 0;
452:         while let Some(idx) = find_cr(&src[search_idx..]) {
453:             if src[search_idx..].get(idx + 1) != Some(&b'\n') {
454:                 search_idx += idx + 1;
455:                 continue;
456:             }
457:             return Some(search_idx + idx);
458:         }
459:         None
460:     }
461: 
462:     fn find_cr(src: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
463:         src.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(idx, &b)| if b == b'\r' { Some(idx) } else { None })
464:     }
465: }

Though the last time I checked this it was caused by the server returning an empty array of hints and responding with a very big latency, I am not sure that this redesign actually fixed #3057....

We didn't handle the case when one rust source file is open in multiple editors in vscode (e.g. by manually adding another editor for the same file or by opening an inline git diff view or just any kind of preview within the same file).

The git diff preview is actually quite special because it causes memory leaks in vscode (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/91782). It is not removed from `visibleEditors` once it is closed. However, this bug doesn't affect the inlay hints anymore, because we don't issue a request and set inlay hints for each editor in isolation. Editors are grouped by their respective files and we issue requests only for files and then update all duplicate editors using the results (so we just update the decorations for already closed git diff preview read-only editors).

Also, note on a hack I had to use. `vscode.TextEdtior` identity is not actually public, its `id` field is not exposed to us. I created a dedicated upstream issue for this (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/91788).

Regarding #3319: the newly designed hints client doesn't issue requests for type hints when switching the visible editors if it has them already cached (though it does rerender things anyway, but this could be optimized in future if so wanted).

    We need to add a postfix completion for `let ... else` syntax, similar to the existing `ifl` (if let) postfix. This will allow users to type `expr.lete` and have it expand to a `let ... else` block with a placeholder for the pattern, the else branch, and the resulting expression.

    1. For `Option` types, add a postfix completion triggered by `lete` that expands to `let Some(...) = expr else { ... };`.
    2. For `Result` types, add a postfix completion triggered by `lete` that expands to `let Ok(...) = expr else { ... };`.

14: pub(super) fn complete_postfix(acc: &mut Completions, ctx: &CompletionContext) {
15:     if !ctx.db.feature_flags.get("completion.enable-postfix") {
16:         return;
17:     }
18: 
19:     let dot_receiver = match &ctx.dot_receiver {
20:         Some(it) => it,
21:         None => return,
22:     };
23: 
24:     let receiver_text = if ctx.dot_receiver_is_ambiguous_float_literal {
25:         let text = dot_receiver.syntax().text();
26:         let without_dot = ..text.len() - TextUnit::of_char('.');
27:         text.slice(without_dot).to_string()
28:     } else {
29:         dot_receiver.syntax().text().to_string()
30:     };
31: 
32:     let receiver_ty = match ctx.sema.type_of_expr(&dot_receiver) {
33:         Some(it) => it,
34:         None => return,
35:     };
36: 
37:     if receiver_ty.is_bool() || receiver_ty.is_unknown() {
38:         postfix_snippet(ctx, "if", "if expr {}", &format!("if {} {{$0}}", receiver_text))
39:             .add_to(acc);
40:         postfix_snippet(
41:             ctx,
42:             "while",
43:             "while expr {}",
44:             &format!("while {} {{\n$0\n}}", receiver_text),
45:         )
46:         .add_to(acc);
47:     }

36: /// Main entry point for completion. We run completion as a two-phase process.
37: ///
38: /// First, we look at the position and collect a so-called `CompletionContext.
39: /// This is a somewhat messy process, because, during completion, syntax tree is
40: /// incomplete and can look really weird.
41: ///
42: /// Once the context is collected, we run a series of completion routines which
43: /// look at the context and produce completion items. One subtlety about this
44: /// phase is that completion engine should not filter by the substring which is
45: /// already present, it should give all possible variants for the identifier at
46: /// the caret. In other words, for
47: ///
48: /// ```no-run
49: /// fn f() {
50: ///     let foo = 92;
51: ///     let _ = bar<|>
52: /// }
53: /// ```
54: ///
55: /// `foo` *should* be present among the completion variants. Filtering by
56: /// identifier prefix/fuzzy match should be done higher in the stack, together
57: /// with ordering of completions (currently this is done by the client).
58: pub(crate) fn completions(db: &RootDatabase, position: FilePosition) -> Option<Completions> {
59:     let ctx = CompletionContext::new(db, position)?;
60: 
61:     let mut acc = Completions::default();
62: 
63:     complete_fn_param::complete_fn_param(&mut acc, &ctx);
64:     complete_keyword::complete_expr_keyword(&mut acc, &ctx);

33:     /// Irrefutable patterns (like let) are excluded.
34:     pub(super) is_pat_binding: bool,
35:     /// A single-indent path, like `foo`. `::foo` should not be considered a trivial path.

38:     pub(super) path_prefix: Option<hir::Path>,

40:     /// `true` if we are a statement or a last expr in the block.
41:     pub(super) can_be_stmt: bool,
42:     /// Something is typed at the "top" level, in module or impl/trait.
43:     pub(super) is_new_item: bool,
44:     /// The receiver if this is a field or method access, i.e. writing something.<|>
45:     pub(super) dot_receiver: Option<ast::Expr>,
46:     pub(super) dot_receiver_is_ambiguous_float_literal: bool,
47:     /// If this is a call (method or function) in particular, i.e. the () are already there.

54:     pub(super) fn new(
55:         db: &'a RootDatabase,
56:         position: FilePosition,
57:     ) -> Option<CompletionContext<'a>> {
58:         let sema = Semantics::new(db);
59: 
60:         let original_file = sema.parse(position.file_id);
61: 
62:         // Insert a fake ident to get a valid parse tree. We will use this file
63:         // to determine context, though the original_file will be used for
64:         // actual completion.

66:             let parse = db.parse(position.file_id);
67:             let edit = AtomTextEdit::insert(position.offset, "intellijRulezz".to_string());
68:             parse.reparse(&edit).tree()
69:         };
70: 
71:         let module = sema.to_module_def(position.file_id);
72:         let token = original_file.syntax().token_at_offset(position.offset).left_biased()?;
73:         let mut ctx = CompletionContext {
74:             sema,
75:             db,
76:             token,
77:             offset: position.offset,
78:             module,
79:             name_ref_syntax: None,
80:             function_syntax: None,
81:             use_item_syntax: None,
82:             record_lit_syntax: None,
83:             record_lit_pat: None,
84:             impl_def: None,
85:             is_param: false,
86:             is_pat_binding: false,
87:             is_trivial_path: false,
88:             path_prefix: None,
89:             after_if: false,
90:             can_be_stmt: false,
91:             is_new_item: false,
92:             dot_receiver: None,
93:             is_call: false,
94:             is_path_type: false,
95:             has_type_args: false,
96:             dot_receiver_is_ambiguous_float_literal: false,
97:         };

2: pub(crate) mod insert_use;
3:

14: pub fn get_missing_impl_items(
15:     sema: &Semantics<RootDatabase>,
16:     impl_def: &ast::ImplDef,
17: ) -> Vec<hir::AssocItem> {
18:     // Names must be unique between constants and functions. However, type aliases
19:     // may share the same name as a function or constant.
20:     let mut impl_fns_consts = FxHashSet::default();
21:     let mut impl_type = FxHashSet::default();
22: 
23:     if let Some(item_list) = impl_def.item_list() {
24:         for item in item_list.impl_items() {
25:             match item {
26:                 ast::ImplItem::FnDef(f) => {
27:                     if let Some(n) = f.name() {
28:                         impl_fns_consts.insert(n.syntax().to_string());
29:                     }
30:                 }
31: 
32:                 ast::ImplItem::TypeAliasDef(t) => {
33:                     if let Some(n) = t.name() {
34:                         impl_type.insert(n.syntax().to_string());
35:                     }
36:                 }
37: 
38:                 ast::ImplItem::ConstDef(c) => {
39:                     if let Some(n) = c.name() {
40:                         impl_fns_consts.insert(n.syntax().to_string());
41:                     }
42:                 }
43:             }
44:         }
45:     }
46: 
47:     resolve_target_trait(sema, impl_def).map_or(vec![], |target_trait| {
48:         target_trait
49:             .items(sema.db)
50:             .iter()
51:             .filter(|i| match i {
52:                 hir::AssocItem::Function(f) => {
53:                     !impl_fns_consts.contains(&f.name(sema.db).to_string())
54:                 }
55:                 hir::AssocItem::TypeAlias(t) => !impl_type.contains(&t.name(sema.db).to_string()),
56:                 hir::AssocItem::Const(c) => c
57:                     .name(sema.db)
58:                     .map(|n| !impl_fns_consts.contains(&n.to_string()))
59:                     .unwrap_or_default(),
60:             })
61:             .cloned()
62:             .collect()
63:     })
64: }
65: 
66: pub(crate) fn resolve_target_trait(
67:     sema: &Semantics<RootDatabase>,
68:     impl_def: &ast::ImplDef,
69: ) -> Option<hir::Trait> {
70:     let ast_path = impl_def
71:         .target_trait()
72:         .map(|it| it.syntax().clone())
73:         .and_then(ast::PathType::cast)?
74:         .path()?;
75: 
76:     match sema.resolve_path(&ast_path) {
77:         Some(hir::PathResolution::Def(hir::ModuleDef::Trait(def))) => Some(def),
78:         _ => None,
79:     }
80: }
81: 
82: pub(crate) fn invert_boolean_expression(expr: ast::Expr) -> ast::Expr {
83:     if let Some(expr) = invert_special_case(&expr) {
84:         return expr;
85:     }
86:     make::expr_prefix(T![!], expr)
87: }
88: 
89: fn invert_special_case(expr: &ast::Expr) -> Option<ast::Expr> {
90:     match expr {
91:         ast::Expr::BinExpr(bin) => match bin.op_kind()? {
92:             ast::BinOp::NegatedEqualityTest => bin.replace_op(T![==]).map(|it| it.into()),
93:             ast::BinOp::EqualityTest => bin.replace_op(T![!=]).map(|it| it.into()),
94:             _ => None,
95:         },
96:         ast::Expr::PrefixExpr(pe) if pe.op_kind()? == ast::PrefixOp::Not => pe.expr(),
97:         // FIXME:
98:         // ast::Expr::Literal(true | false )
99:         _ => None,
100:     }
101: }

2: //! actions (in LSP) or intentions (in IntelliJ).

4: //! An assist is a micro-refactoring, which is automatically activated in
5: //! certain context. For example, if the cursor is over `,`, a "swap `,`" assist
6: //! becomes available.

61: /// Return all the assists applicable at the given position.

63: /// Assists are returned in the "unresolved" state, that is only labels are
64: /// returned, without actual edits.
65: pub fn unresolved_assists(db: &RootDatabase, range: FileRange) -> Vec<AssistLabel> {
66:     let sema = Semantics::new(db);

69:         .iter()

86:         .flat_map(|it| it.0)

47: /// `AssistCtx` allows to apply an assist or check if it could be applied.
48: ///
49: /// Assists use a somewhat over-engineered approach, given the current needs. The
50: /// assists workflow consists of two phases. In the first phase, a user asks for
51: /// the list of available assists. In the second phase, the user picks a
52: /// particular assist and it gets applied.
53: ///
54: /// There are two peculiarities here:
55: ///
56: /// * first, we ideally avoid computing more things then necessary to answer
57: ///   "is assist applicable" in the first phase.
58: /// * second, when we are applying assist, we don't have a guarantee that there
59: ///   weren't any changes between the point when user asked for assists and when
60: ///   they applied a particular assist. So, when applying assist, we need to do
61: ///   all the checks from scratch.
62: ///
63: /// To avoid repeating the same code twice for both "check" and "apply"
64: /// functions, we use an approach reminiscent of that of Django's function based
65: /// views dealing with forms. Each assist receives a runtime parameter,
66: /// `should_compute_edit`. It first check if an edit is applicable (potentially
67: /// computing info required to compute the actual edit). If it is applicable,
68: /// and `should_compute_edit` is `true`, it then computes the actual edit.

71: /// with `should_compute_edit = false`, and then applying the selected edit
72: /// again, with `should_compute_edit = true` this time.

75: /// moment, because the LSP API is pretty awkward in this place, and it's much

93: /// Check whether the node is a valid expression which can be extracted to a variable.
94: /// In general that's true for any expression, but in some cases that would produce invalid code.
95: fn valid_target_expr(node: SyntaxNode) -> Option<ast::Expr> {
96:     match node.kind() {
97:         PATH_EXPR | LOOP_EXPR => None,
98:         BREAK_EXPR => ast::BreakExpr::cast(node).and_then(|e| e.expr()),
99:         RETURN_EXPR => ast::ReturnExpr::cast(node).and_then(|e| e.expr()),
100:         BLOCK_EXPR => {
101:             ast::BlockExpr::cast(node).filter(|it| it.is_standalone()).map(ast::Expr::from)
102:         }
103:         _ => ast::Expr::cast(node),
104:     }
105: }

107: /// Returns the syntax node which will follow the freshly introduced var
108: /// and a boolean indicating whether we have to wrap it within a { } block
109: /// to produce correct code.
110: /// It can be a statement, the last in a block expression or a wanna be block
111: /// expression like a lambda or match arm.
112: fn anchor_stmt(expr: ast::Expr) -> Option<(SyntaxNode, bool)> {
113:     expr.syntax().ancestors().find_map(|node| {
114:         if let Some(expr) = node.parent().and_then(ast::Block::cast).and_then(|it| it.expr()) {
115:             if expr.syntax() == &node {
116:                 tested_by!(test_introduce_var_last_expr);
117:                 return Some((node, false));
118:             }
119:         }
120: 
121:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
122:             if parent.kind() == MATCH_ARM || parent.kind() == LAMBDA_EXPR {
123:                 return Some((node, true));
124:             }
125:         }
126: 
127:         if ast::Stmt::cast(node.clone()).is_some() {
128:             return Some((node, false));
129:         }
130: 
131:         None
132:     })
133: }

20:     doc: String,
21:     before: String,
22:     after: String,
23: }
24: 
25: fn hide_hash_comments(text: &str) -> String {
26:     text.split('\n') // want final newline
27:         .filter(|&it| !(it.starts_with("# ") || it == "#"))
28:         .map(|it| format!("{}\n", it))
29:         .collect()
30: }
31: 
32: fn reveal_hash_comments(text: &str) -> String {
33:     text.split('\n') // want final newline
34:         .map(|it| {
35:             if it.starts_with("# ") {
36:                 &it[2..]
37:             } else if it == "#" {
38:                 ""
39:             } else {
40:                 it
41:             }
42:         })
43:         .map(|it| format!("{}\n", it))
44:         .collect()
45: }

47: fn collect_assists() -> Result<Vec<Assist>> {
48:     let mut res = Vec::new();
49:     for entry in fs::read_dir(project_root().join(codegen::ASSISTS_DIR))? {
50:         let entry = entry?;
51:         let path = entry.path();
52:         if path.is_file() {
53:             collect_file(&mut res, path.as_path())?;
54:         }
55:     }
56:     res.sort_by(|lhs, rhs| lhs.id.cmp(&rhs.id));
57:     return Ok(res);
58: 
59:     fn collect_file(acc: &mut Vec<Assist>, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
60:         let text = fs::read_to_string(path)?;
61:         let comment_blocks = extract_comment_blocks_with_empty_lines(&text);
62: 
63:         for block in comment_blocks {
64:             // FIXME: doesn't support blank lines yet, need to tweak
65:             // `extract_comment_blocks` for that.
66:             let mut lines = block.iter();
67:             let first_line = lines.next().unwrap();
68:             if !first_line.starts_with("Assist: ") {
69:                 continue;
70:             }
71:             let id = first_line["Assist: ".len()..].to_string();
72:             assert!(
73:                 id.chars().all(|it| it.is_ascii_lowercase() || it == '_'),
74:                 "invalid assist id: {:?}",
75:                 id
76:             );
77: 
78:             let doc = take_until(lines.by_ref(), "```").trim().to_string();
79:             assert!(
80:                 doc.chars().next().unwrap().is_ascii_uppercase() && doc.ends_with('.'),
81:                 "\n\n{}: assist docs should be proper sentences, with capitalization and a full stop at the end.\n\n{}\n\n",
82:                 id, doc,
83:             );
84: 
85:             let before = take_until(lines.by_ref(), "```");
86: 
87:             assert_eq!(lines.next().unwrap().as_str(), "->");
88:             assert_eq!(lines.next().unwrap().as_str(), "```");
89:             let after = take_until(lines.by_ref(), "```");
90:             acc.push(Assist { id, doc, before, after })

93:         fn take_until<'a>(lines: impl Iterator<Item = &'a String>, marker: &str) -> String {
94:             let mut buf = Vec::new();
95:             for line in lines {
96:                 if line == marker {
97:                     break;
98:                 }
99:                 buf.push(line.clone());
100:             }
101:             buf.join("\n")
102:         }
103:         Ok(())
104:     }
105: }

21: // Promotes a local variable to a const item changing its name to a `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` variant
22: // if the local uses no non-const expressions.

47: pub(crate) fn promote_local_to_const(acc: &mut Assists, ctx: &AssistContext<'_>) -> Option<()> {
48:     let pat = ctx.find_node_at_offset::<ast::IdentPat>()?;
49:     let name = pat.name()?;
50:     if !pat.is_simple_ident() {
51:         cov_mark::hit!(promote_local_non_simple_ident);
52:         return None;
53:     }
54:     let let_stmt = pat.syntax().parent().and_then(ast::LetStmt::cast)?;
55: 
56:     let module = ctx.sema.scope(pat.syntax())?.module();
57:     let local = ctx.sema.to_def(&pat)?;
58:     let ty = ctx.sema.type_of_pat(&pat.into())?.original;
59: 
60:     let ty = match ty.display_source_code(ctx.db(), module.into(), false) {
61:         Ok(ty) => ty,
62:         Err(_) => {
63:             cov_mark::hit!(promote_local_not_applicable_if_ty_not_inferred);
64:             return None;
65:         }
66:     };
67: 
68:     let initializer = let_stmt.initializer()?;
69:     if !is_body_const(&ctx.sema, &initializer) {
70:         cov_mark::hit!(promote_local_non_const);
71:         return None;
72:     }
73: 
74:     acc.add(
75:         AssistId("promote_local_to_const", AssistKind::Refactor),
76:         "Promote local to constant",
77:         let_stmt.syntax().text_range(),
78:         |edit| {
79:             let name = to_upper_snake_case(&name.to_string());
80:             let usages = Definition::Local(local).usages(&ctx.sema).all();
81:             if let Some(usages) = usages.references.get(&ctx.file_id()) {
82:                 let name_ref = make::name_ref(&name);
83: 
84:                 for usage in usages {
85:                     let Some(usage_name) = usage.name.as_name_ref().cloned() else { continue };
86:                     if let Some(record_field) = ast::RecordExprField::for_name_ref(&usage_name) {
87:                         let name_expr = make::expr_path(make::path_from_text(&name));
88:                         utils::replace_record_field_expr(ctx, edit, record_field, name_expr);
89:                     } else {
90:                         let usage_range = usage.range;
91:                         edit.replace(usage_range, name_ref.syntax().text());
92:                     }
93:                 }
94:             }
95: 
96:             let item = make::item_const(None, make::name(&name), make::ty(&ty), initializer)
97:                 .clone_for_update();
98:             let let_stmt = edit.make_mut(let_stmt);
99: 
100:             if let Some((cap, name)) = ctx.config.snippet_cap.zip(item.name()) {
101:                 edit.add_tabstop_before(cap, name);
102:             }
103: 
104:             ted::replace(let_stmt.syntax(), item.syntax());
105:         },
106:     )
107: }

109: fn is_body_const(sema: &Semantics<'_, RootDatabase>, expr: &ast::Expr) -> bool {
110:     let mut is_const = true;
111:     preorder_expr(expr, &mut |ev| {
112:         let expr = match ev {
113:             WalkEvent::Enter(_) if !is_const => return true,
114:             WalkEvent::Enter(expr) => expr,
115:             WalkEvent::Leave(_) => return false,
116:         };
117:         match expr {
118:             ast::Expr::CallExpr(call) => {
119:                 if let Some(ast::Expr::PathExpr(path_expr)) = call.expr() {
120:                     if let Some(PathResolution::Def(ModuleDef::Function(func))) =
121:                         path_expr.path().and_then(|path| sema.resolve_path(&path))
122:                     {
123:                         is_const &= func.is_const(sema.db);
124:                     }
125:                 }
126:             }
127:             ast::Expr::MethodCallExpr(call) => {
128:                 is_const &=
129:                     sema.resolve_method_call(&call).map(|it| it.is_const(sema.db)).unwrap_or(true)
130:             }
131:             ast::Expr::ForExpr(_)
132:             | ast::Expr::ReturnExpr(_)
133:             | ast::Expr::TryExpr(_)
134:             | ast::Expr::YieldExpr(_)
135:             | ast::Expr::AwaitExpr(_) => is_const = false,
136:             _ => (),
137:         }
138:         !is_const
139:     });
140:     is_const
141: }
